Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said the "humanitarian catastrophe" in Gaza and the failure to ensure accountability for the Israeli military's "excessive use of force" were undermining public support even in nations supportive of Israel. "Partnership requires mutual respect," Sikorski said on Thursday on US social media company X. "The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for [Israel Defence Forces] IDF's excessive use of force, are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations," he added. His comments came as Poland's Foreign Ministry expressed "great disappointment" over Israeli military authorities' decision to discontinue proceedings into the April 1, 2024 shelling of a World Central Kitchen humanitarian aid convoy in the Gaza Strip that killed Polish citizen Damian Sobol. The ministry said the Israeli ambassador in Warsaw was summoned following the decision, which Poland was informed of on August 19. https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.text: Today’s fertiliser shortage could become tomorrow’s food crisis, commerce minister Piyush Goyal said at the G20 trade ministers’ meeting in Milwaukee, and on its sidelines he also held a “productive” discussion with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on early conclusion of the proposed India-US trade deal.“Met USTR Jamieson Greer, @USTradeRep, on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee. Had a productive discussion with USTR Greer towards early conclusion of a mutually beneficial interim agreement under the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement,” Goyal said in a post on X. India and the US are engaged in talks to finalise the proposed interim bilateral trade agreement (BTA) in line with the joint statement issued on February 7. Although the two had reached a framework for an interim BTA in February, they could not sign the agreement after the US Supreme Court invalidated the legal basis for the preferential tariff mechanism Washington had offered. India is now awaiting a preferential tariff framework that provides competitive access for its exporters vis-a-vis competing countries.Also Read I US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.34%, highest since 2002: Why are yields rising? G20 chairship, food security“We also exchanged views on G20 deliberations under US Chairship,” Goyal said in the post. He also participated in the opening day of the G20 trade ministers’ meeting, hosted under the United States G20 Presidency. Speaking at the session on food and trade, Goyal thanked the Presidency for placing food at the centre of the discussions.“Ensuring food security for all and creating greater opportunities for farmers are central to India’s policy and food must never be used as an instrument of pressure against any country,” a commerce ministry’s statement quoted minister as saying on Thursday. Countries of the Global South are among the most adversely impacted by the food, fuel and fertiliser crises caused by global conflicts, the minister added.Goyal said during the Covid-19 pandemic, India ensured food security for over 1.4 billion citizens and supplied foodgrains to several countries in need. He noted that over 800 million people in India are currently being provided foodgrains free of cost.Also Read I Piyush Goyal pushes for bid to strengthen India-US ties at business roundtableIndia maintains public stockholding (PSH), procures from small and marginal farmers and, in the event of a harvest shortfall, adopts temporary and transparent measures to ensure the availability and affordability of food, Goyal said. “These measures are recognised under the WTO, including through the Bali Ministerial Decision and the Geneva Ministerial Declaration,” the statement quoting him said.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck20.text: Image source, Getty Images By Dan Johnson ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Olga Malchevska Published 27 October 2026, 02:58 GMT Updated 9 minutes ago A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity. Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday. Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces. Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave. There are concerns that truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity." Up to 6,000 people including 200 children remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, Kyiv believes, with only 1,700 still living in the city itself. Before the war it was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape is highly dangerous because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack. No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water for three years. Pope Leo XIV appealed earlier this month to Russia's Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire. The current truce is supposed to allow supplies in and enable roads to be cleared of mines to allow people safe passage out in an evacuation planned to take place on Friday. One woman told the BBC she had stepped on a land mine and was currently in hospital where she had undergone two operations. "I don't know how long I will have to spend there," she said, worried about not being able to join the evacuation. It is hard to make contact with people in Oleshky as communication is patchy and and many are reluctant to speak of the situation in fear of reprisals from the Russians, making it difficult to verify reports the ceasefire is being implemented. Many details on the evacuation plans are unclear, initially including how and where to register for it. Some people want to know if they can bring their pets. Others are questioning what future they will have if they opt to leave their homes. "It is critically important that this mission to rescue our people proceeds successfully and safely," Kyrylo Budanov, the head of Zelensky's office, said on Tuesday. Russia's defence ministry said units from the army's Dnepr group had been conducting "engineering reconnaissance" and clearing main access roads into the village of "explosive and booby-trap devices". While people are optimistic about leaving, there are also fears that Russia may not allow them to return to Ukraine, or examine their phones and online activity for signs of Ukrainian support, which could see them be taken away and tortured. Someone who has been speaking to family in Oleshky said they fear shooting could restart during evacuations and Ukraine will somehow be blamed for not upholding the truce. Image source, Ksenia Arkhipova Image caption, These residents were able to get out of Oleshky in spring this year Last month, the Kremlin acknowledged that Oleshky faced "a critical situation" and "problems with supplies of food and medicine", but added that "Russia's military was working to resolve them" and blamed Kyiv. In response to the situation, the White House said last week that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire, with no details for how long it would last. Russia's defence ministry said on Telegram it had stopped firing toward the Ukrainian city of Kherson - across the river from Oleshky - at 04:00 Moscow time (01:00 GMT) in preparation for the humanitarian operation. Ukrainian officials say parliament's commissioner for human rights, Dmytro Lubinets, has travelled to the areas to co-ordinate the operation. "This is part of a humanitarian mission being carried out with the mediation and co-ordination of US First Lady Melania Trump, in co-operation with Yana Lantratova, Russia's Commissioner for Human Rights," Lubinets wrote on social media. Ukraine's military general staff said that silence was being observed over the operation for humanitarian purposes, and urged people not to trust unverified reports or spread rumours about "the routes, time and place of the movement of people and humanitarian convoys". Image source, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets Image caption, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and its people are now trapped Zelensky has warned that routes out of Oleshky that are demined by Russia will ensure that those civilians leaving Oleshky will "head towards Russia and stay there". However, he said some would get to Ukrainian-controlled territory "one way or another", and ideally anyone trapped would be able to reach their destination and evacuate to Ukraine. The White House said in the statement last week that "non-military, civilian leaders from both countries would work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require". While the US first lady is relatively lower profile than some of her predecessors - and only occasionally seen at White House events - she has become involved in addressing humanitarian issues stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war. In August 2025, she penned a letter to Putin, telling him it was "time to protect children and future generations worldwide". While a truce is under way in Oleshky, elsewhere strikes continue. On Monday evening, attacks on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv hit a university and a bridge, killing one person and injuring 14 others. In Russia, one person was killed and six others were injured after a Ukrainian drone strike on Bryansk. https://www.kyivpost.com/post/87372.text: War Ukraine World North America Latin America Europe Eastern Europe Middle East Africa Asia Economy Business Technology Finance Energy Agriculture Videos Podcasts Analysis Corruption Watch Opinions Culture Reviews History Sports Classifieds Spotlight Cartoons EN UK NATO Europe Poland Europe Readies Post-Truce Ukraine Deployment Drill In brief: At least 1,500 military personnel from Britain, France, and Germany will deploy to Poland in November to conduct joint maneuvers rehearsing troop deployments and logistics in Ukraine in the event of a ceasefire. Announced by UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting following Pentagon talks, the exercise focuses on military training, logistics sustainment, and post-war deterrence without deploying troops immediately. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 17, 2026, 3:26 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied French soldiers operate a Caesar Mk-I wheeled self-propelled howitzer during a live fire exercise of Lithuanian and French troops along with NATO allies at the General Silvestras Zukauskas Training Area in Pabrade, Lithuania, Sept. 16, 2026. (Photo by Petras Malukas / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip At least 1,500 military personnel from the UK , France , and Germany will deploy to Poland in November to conduct specialized joint exercises simulating troop deployment and stabilization procedures in Ukraine in the event of a negotiated ceasefire, The Times reported. The multinational maneuvers were formally announced by UK Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting following bilateral consultations with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Pentagon on Thursday, Oct. 15. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Streeting confirmed that “hundreds” of British soldiers will participate in the deployment exercise alongside European counterparts. “Next month, thousands of military personnel will take part in major exercises in Poland to ensure that we are ready to support the military training and post-war reconstruction that Ukraine will need,” Streeting stated. Advertisement According to defense sources cited by The Times, the exercise marks the first dedicated allied simulation designed specifically to prepare for a post-conflict phase in Ukraine, where the physical presence of European forces would serve as a conventional deterrent against renewed aggression. Logistics, training, and deterrence protocols Participating formations will rehearse cross-border transit logistics, rapid re-supply chains, and baseline sustainment operations – including forward food and fuel pipelines – under the framework of a prospective multinational peacekeeping or training commitment. Other Topics of Interest EU Tasks Commission to Bridge Ukraine’s €70B Funding Gap EU leaders have directed the European Commission to draft plans covering Ukraine’s €70B gap, as Macron pledges European satellite aid. Defense officials emphasized that the maneuvers do not indicate an imminent deployment of NATO troops into Ukrainian sovereign territory. Instead, the exercise is engineered to validate technical protocols and joint command interoperability should a durable armistice or cessation of hostilities materialize . The initiative highlights expanding coordination among European defense ministries to assume greater responsibility for continental security frameworks and wartime transition contingencies, ensuring rapid response capabilities if a ceasefire is formalized between Kyiv and Moscow . Advertisement Black Sea security requests and maritime friction The planning for post-conflict deployment rehearsals in Poland arrives as NATO’s eastern and southeastern frontiers confront mounting operational challenges and maritime security friction. Meanwhile, Bulgaria requested expanded defensive assistance from NATO on Oct. 16, asking the alliance to supply combat aircraft, air defense missile batteries, counter-unmanned aerial vehicle (C-UAV) systems, and regular air patrols following repeated drone attacks against merchant shipping transiting its Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov confirmed that Sofia requested “the entire spectrum of available assets” to reinforce deterrence in the region, noting that regional partners Romania and the Baltic states confront comparable aerial and maritime vulnerabilities. The security appeals followed consecutive drone strikes targeting civilian commercial shipping off the Bulgarian coastline throughout October. On Oct. 6, strikes hit the commercial vessels Alfa Watan and Able within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, causing the Alfa Watan to sink and marking the first hostile kinetic attack inside the maritime economic perimeter of a NATO member state. Advertisement Subsequent strikes on Oct. 13 damaged the Maltese-flagged cargo vessel Chelsea 3 roughly 18 nautical miles off Byala and sank a second vessel near Krapets, prompting Bulgarian authorities to deploy additional missile batteries and drone-tracking systems along the coastline.
